text:
incident-bot: PAGE — Automated alert: sustained spike in 5xx for Thalassa (enterprise / dedicated pool thalassa-prod-vpc) in us-east. Error rate 5m avg 12% (baseline <1%). Runbook: regional-traffic-shift. Paging ashwin, haley, dylan. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/regional-traffic-shift

ashwin (oncall): on it. can someone confirm customer-visible impact? are they seeing increased latency or errors from their side?

maria (customer-eng): Thalassa SRE just pinged via support channel — reporting ~30% of sessions in us-east returning 502/timeout. They asked for a staged reroute, not a hard cut. Customer prefers minimal session loss.

haley (sre): thanks @maria. quick checks: pool thalassa-prod-vpc has 2 hot nodes in us-east, us-east metrics show queuing on the router tier. warm capacity in us-west looks idle: 4 reserved nodes. we should avoid full DNS swap; propose traffic steering by weight to us-west first, TTL drop for quick rollback.

dylan (infra): agree. preparing to provision ephemeral warm instances if needed. current plan: 1) lower DNS TTL for customer CNAME to 30s 2) apply routing policy: 20% -> us-west, 80% -> us-east 3) monitor 10m, 50% if stable, then 100% only if errors go to baseline.

ashwin (oncall): sound plan. @adrian please notify Thalassa PM we're doing a staged shift and will escalate if any session loss.

adrian (acctmgr): pinged customer (email + support channel): "We are initiating a staged traffic shift to mitigate increased errors in us-east. Expect brief reconnections. We'll keep you posted." they acknowledged and asked for timing windows — said now is okay.

ops-runner: prepping commands. dropping snippets here for visibility.

```bash
# check pool status
rctl pool status thalassa-prod-vpc --region us-east
rctl pool status thalassa-prod-vpc --region us-west

# reduce customer CNAME TTL
dnsctl set-ttl thalassa.example.cname 30

# apply weight-based routing in control plane
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-west --weight 20
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-east --weight 80

# rollback (if needed)
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-west --weight 0
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-east --weight 100
```

dylan (infra): running the checks now, will post outputs.

ashwin (oncall): @dylan please also capture a short tcpdump of ingress to confirm errors are not client-side. share artifacts in thread.

dylan (infra): pasted quick outputs (summarized): us-east router queues high, 25% CPU on model workers spiking with long tail p95+k spikes. us-west workers idle. initiating TTL change and applying 20% weight to us-west now.

incident-bot: UPDATE — TTL change applied for thalassa.example.cname -> 30s. routing policy updated: 20% us-west, 80% us-east.

maria (customer-eng): customer reports a drop in 502s to ~12% (from 30%). they appreciate the gradual approach.

haley (sre): running synthetic checks against both regions. initial synthetic success rate: us-west 99.7%, us-east 88.1. monitoring logs for 5xx trend. recommend preparing to push to 50% in 10 minutes if slope continues down.

ashwin (oncall): agreed. timeline: 10m observation, if errors <=3% then increase to 50%. if errors plateau above 5% rollback to us-east 100% and re-evaluate.

dylan (infra): queuing autoscale jobs for us-west hot pool - provisioning two ephemeral workers now: `rctl pool provision --name thalassa-prod-vpc --region us-west --count 2 --type ephemeral`. ETA ~150s.

ops-runner: note — session affinity could cause some user sessions to keep hitting us-east until DNS TTL expires. session cookie TTL for Thalassa is 60s; important to watch for reconnect storms.

adrian (acctmgr): relaying note to customer: "We are increasing traffic to us-west in stages and monitoring closely; may see a brief reconnection window as sessions rebalance."

incident-bot: ALERT — at +9m after shift, us-east 5xx down to 6%, overall user impact reduced ~80%. continuing to monitor.

haley (sre): proceeding to 50% weight now. applying command.

```bash
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-west --weight 50
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-east --weight 50
```

incident-bot: UPDATE — routing policy: 50/50.

maria (customer-eng): customer reports errors now ~2-3% — nearly back to normal. they asked when we will return to normal topology.

ashwin (oncall): recommendation: keep 50/50 for 15m to ensure stability, then either return 100% to us-west (if we've validated state parity) or set to 100% us-east if we decide to reinstate original region. we should not DNS-cutover until backend state sync is confirmed. haley please confirm stateful services parity (KV caches, model weights).

haley (sre): model weights OK, KV cache lag small but within acceptable window (~30s behind). we'll run a background sync job now.

dylan (infra): ephemeral workers in us-west are healthy and registered. no increased error rates from them.

incident-bot: NOTE — autoscale action completed: 2 ephemeral workers provisioned in us-west.

ops-runner: prepared rollback commands and runbook snippet once more for visibility.

```bash
# immediate rollback to east-only
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-west --weight 0
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-east --weight 100
# reset TTL after rollback
dnsctl set-ttl thalassa.example.cname 300
```

ashwin (oncall): all right — maintain 50/50 for 15m, continue synthetic checks and customer monitor. @adrian keep customer PM updated with 15m status.

incident-bot: UPDATE (15m stable at 50/50) — us-east 5xx now 1.1%, overall error rate within SLA.

maria (customer-eng): customer confirms normal behavior and thanks the team. they requested a post-incident note.

haley (sre): proceeding to move traffic to us-west 100% only after final parity check completes (expected ~3m). will then optionally initiate DNS CNAME point change to prefer us-west origin and increase TTL to 300s.

dylan (infra): parity check complete. KV lag cleared. executing full weight flip to us-west.

```bash
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-west --weight 100
redwood route set-weight --customer thalassa --region us-east --weight 0
dnsctl set-ttl thalassa.example.cname 300
```

incident-bot: RESOLVED — Traffic successfully migrated to us-west for Thalassa. Incident closed by ashwin (oncall). Summary: staged weight shift + ephemeral capacity prevented provider-level outage and avoided full DNS cutover until safe. postmortem requested.

ashwin (oncall): closing the incident. will file a postmortem and include timeline, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (improve autoscale thresholds, add pre-warm playbook). thanks team :thumbsup:

adrian (acctmgr): customer follow-up scheduled.

haley (sre): follow-ups: 1) tune router queue alert to trigger earlier 2) add a one-click route rollback button in console 3) document session-affinity caveats.

maria (customer-eng): i'll coordinate the post-incident write-up with the customer-facing summary.

ops-runner: artifacts: tcpdump + spm graphs uploaded to /artifacts/incidents/2919008765/

incident-bot: THREAD LOCKED — routine follow-ups moved to #postmortems and internal ticketing.
